title: The Obvious Step for Understanding Others
author: Greg McKeown
summary: McKeown frames misunderstanding as rooted not in lack of intuition but in our failure to ask. A landmark study shows even spouses are no better than strangers at decoding ambiguous statements. Proximity creates confidence without accuracy. The embarrassingly simple solution: ask what matters most, what could improve, what they need. Leaders miss this obvious step constantly, preferring to assume customer needs, team struggles, and gift preferences rather than direct inquiry.
points: Relationship confidence can increase without corresponding gains in actual accuracy.
Most leaders resort to guessing instead of asking people directly.
Direct questions reveal the friction points that teams experience daily.
Even spouses are no more accurate than complete strangers at interpretation.
This obvious principle transforms customer, team, and family working relationships.
quotes: If you want to know how someone feels then ask them.
We don't misunderstand because we lack intuition. We misunderstand because we don't ASK.
The relationship actually increased CONFIDENCE, not ACCURACY at understanding them.

We spend hours, days, months trying to get inside their head when we could just ask them. Asking works better than guessing what people really want from you.” Archived from 1-Minute Wednesday Newsletter on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
